message.content:
[ISSUE #1] [SEVERITY: Critical] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)]
Description: The "Username" and "Password" input fields have placeholder text with insufficient contrast against the dark background. The placeholder text appears to be a light gray (#888888 or similar) on a black background (#000000), resulting in a contrast ratio of approximately 2.5:1, which is below the required 4.5:1 for normal text.
Impact: Users with visual impairments, particularly those with low vision or color blindness, will struggle to read the placeholder text, making it difficult to understand what information is required in each field.
Fix: Change the placeholder text color to a shade with a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the input background. For example, use `#FFFFFF` (white) or `#E0E0E0` (light gray) for the placeholder text. Ensure the contrast ratio is calculated using the actual background color of the input field.

[ISSUE #2] [SEVERITY: Critical] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)]
Description: The "REGISTER" button has text with insufficient contrast against its dark gray background. The text appears to be a light gray (#CCCCCC or similar) on a dark gray background (#333333), resulting in a contrast ratio of approximately 3.5:1, which is below the required 4.5:1 for normal text.
Impact: Users with visual impairments will have difficulty reading the text on the "REGISTER" button, potentially causing them to miss this option or misinterpret its purpose.
Fix: Change the "REGISTER" button text color to a shade with a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the button background. For example, use `#FFFFFF` (white) for the text.

[ISSUE #3] [SEVERITY: Critical] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 2.1.1 Keyboard]
Description: The "Username" and "Password" input fields lack visible focus indicators. When a user tabs to these fields, there is no visual change (e.g., border color, outline, or background highlight) to indicate which field is currently focused.
Impact: Keyboard-only users and screen reader users will be unable to determine which input field is active, leading to confusion and potential input errors.
Fix: Add a visible focus indicator to all input fields. For example, apply a `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #4CAF50;` or `border: 1px solid #4CAF50;` to the focused input field. Ensure the focus indicator has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent colors.

[ISSUE #4] [SEVERITY: Critical] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 2.4.7 Focus Visible]
Description: Interactive elements such as the "LOGIN", "REGISTER", and "CONNECT" buttons lack visible focus indicators. When a user tabs to these buttons, there is no visual change (e.g., border, outline, or background highlight) to indicate which button is currently focused.
Impact: Keyboard-only users and screen reader users will be unable to determine which button is active, leading to confusion and potential interaction errors.
Fix: Add a visible focus indicator to all interactive buttons. For example, apply a `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #4CAF50;` or `border: 1px solid #4CAF50;` to the focused button. Ensure the focus indicator has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent colors.

[ISSUE #5] [SEVERITY: High] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value]
Description: The "Username" and "Password" input fields lack associated labels. The placeholder text is used as a label, but this is not an accessible practice.
Impact: Screen reader users will not hear the label for these input fields, making it unclear what information is expected in each field.
Fix: Add `<label>` elements associated with each input field using the `for` attribute. For example: `<label for="username">Username</label>` and `<label for="password">Password</label>`. Ensure the labels are visually hidden or positioned appropriately so they do not disrupt the layout.

[ISSUE #6] [SEVERITY: High] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions]
Description: The "Username" and "Password" input fields lack visible labels. The placeholder text is used as a label, but this is not an accessible practice and disappears once the user starts typing.
Impact: Users may be confused about what information is required in each field, especially if they need to reference the label again after starting to type.
Fix: Add visible labels above or to the left of each input field. For example: `<label for="username">Username</label>` and `<label for="password">Password</label>`. Ensure the labels are clearly associated with their respective input fields.

[ISSUE #7] [SEVERITY: High] [FRAMEWORK: Nielsen] [CRITERION: 3. User Control and Freedom]
Description: There is no "Cancel" or "Close" button visible on the "IDK Network" login modal. Users who accidentally opened this modal or changed their mind may not have an easy way to exit without logging in or registering.
Impact: Users may feel trapped in the modal, leading to frustration and potential abandonment of the launcher.
Fix: Add a "Cancel" or "Close" button to the modal. This button should close the modal and return the user to the previous screen. Place it in a logical location, such as next to the "LOGIN" button or in the top-right corner of the modal.

[ISSUE #8] [SEVERITY: Medium] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast]
Description: The "LOGIN" button has a green background (#4CAF50 or similar) with white text (#FFFFFF), which meets the 4.5:1 contrast ratio. However, the "REGISTER" button has a dark gray background (#333333 or similar) with light gray text (#CCCCCC), resulting in a contrast ratio of approximately 3.5:1, which is below the required 3:1 for non-text contrast.
Impact: Users with visual impairments may have difficulty distinguishing the "REGISTER" button from the background, making it harder to interact with.
Fix: Increase the contrast of the "REGISTER" button text or background. For example, change the text color to `#FFFFFF` (white) or the background color to a lighter gray to achieve a contrast ratio of at least 3:1.

[ISSUE #9] [SEVERITY: Medium] [FRAMEWORK: Nielsen] [CRITERION: 9. Help Users Recognize, Diagnose, and Recover from Errors]
Description: There are no visible error messages or validation feedback for the "Username" and "Password" input fields. If a user enters invalid credentials or leaves a field empty, they will not receive immediate feedback.
Impact: Users may submit the form multiple times without knowing why it failed, leading to frustration and confusion.
Fix: Implement real-time validation and error messaging. Display clear, concise error messages below the input fields when validation fails (e.g., "Username is required" or "Password is incorrect"). Use color and icons to draw attention to errors.

[ISSUE #10] [SEVERITY: Medium] [FRAMEWORK: LawOfUX] [CRITERION: Fitts's Law]
Description: The "CONNECT" button is relatively small and may be difficult for users to target, especially on lower-resolution screens or with imprecise input methods (e.g., touchscreens).
Impact: Users may accidentally miss the "CONNECT" button or have difficulty clicking it, leading to interaction errors.
Fix: Increase the size of the "CONNECT" button to meet Fitts's Law recommendations. Ensure the button has a minimum height of 44px and a minimum width of 80px. Increase the padding and font size to make it more targetable.

[ISSUE #11] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: Nielsen] [CRITERION: 2. Consistency and Standards]
Description: The "LOGIN" button is green, while the "REGISTER" button is dark gray. This color scheme is inconsistent and may confuse users about the primary action.
Impact: Users may be unsure which button is the primary action (login) and which is the secondary action (register).
Fix: Use a consistent color scheme for buttons. For example, make both the "LOGIN" and "REGISTER" buttons green, with the "LOGIN" button having a more prominent style (e.g., bolder, larger) to indicate it is the primary action.

[ISSUE #12] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: LawOfUX] [CRITERION: Law of Proximity]
Description: The "Username" and "Password" input fields are placed close together, but the "CONNECT" button is separated by a larger gap. This may disrupt the visual flow and make the form feel less cohesive.
Impact: Users may perceive the form as less organized and have to scan more to find the "CONNECT" button.
Fix: Reduce the vertical spacing between the "Password" input field and the "CONNECT" button to match the spacing between the other form elements. Ensure consistent padding and margins throughout the form.

[ISSUE #13] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: LawOfUX] [CRITERION: Law of Common Region]
Description: The "IDK Network" login form elements (title, description, buttons, inputs) are grouped together, but the background is a solid black color, which may not clearly define the form's boundaries.
Impact: The form may feel less distinct from the rest of the launcher interface, making it harder for users to focus on the login process.
Fix: Add a subtle background color or border to the form to create a common region. For example, use a dark gray background (#1E1E1E) with a 1px border (#333333) to clearly define the form area.

[ISSUE #14] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus]
Description: The "LOGIN" and "REGISTER" buttons do not have distinct hover or active states. When a user hovers over or clicks these buttons, there is no visual feedback.
Impact: Users may not be sure if their interaction was successful, leading to uncertainty and potential repeated clicks.
Fix: Add hover and active states to all interactive buttons. For example, on hover, change the background color to a lighter shade of green (#66BB6A) and on active, change it to an even lighter shade (#81C784). Ensure the text color remains accessible.

[ISSUE #15] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: Nielsen] [CRITERION: 1. Visibility of System Status]
Description: There is no loading indicator or feedback when the user clicks the "CONNECT" button. Users may not know if the login process is in progress or if the button was clicked.
Impact: Users may click the "CONNECT" button multiple times, thinking it didn't register, or become impatient and abandon the process.
Fix: Add a loading indicator (e.g., a spinner or progress bar) to the "CONNECT" button or next to it when the login process is in progress. Change the button text to "Connecting..." or similar to provide feedback.

[ISSUE #16] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: LawOfUX] [CRITERION: Miller's Law]
Description: The form contains multiple elements (title, description, two buttons, two inputs, one main button), which may overwhelm users and make the login process feel more complex than it is.
Impact: Users may feel overwhelmed by the number of elements and make more errors.
Fix: Simplify the form by reducing the number of elements. For example, remove the "LOGIN" and "REGISTER" buttons and use a single "Connect" button that handles both login and registration based on the presence of credentials. Alternatively, use a tabbed interface to separate login and registration.

[ISSUE #17] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 2.4.3 Focus Order]
Description: The tab order of the form elements may not be logical. For example, the "LOGIN" button may be focused before the "Username" input field.
Impact: Keyboard users may have to tab through multiple elements to reach the input fields, leading to a less efficient interaction.
Fix: Ensure the tab order follows a logical sequence: "Username" input, "Password" input, "CONNECT" button, "LOGIN" button, "REGISTER" button. Use the `tabindex` attribute to control the focus order if necessary.

[ISSUE #18] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: Nielsen] [CRITERION: 8. Aesthetic and Minimalist Design]
Description: The "IDK Network" title uses a pixelated font, which may be visually distracting and inconsistent with the rest of the launcher's design.
Impact: The pixelated font may make the title harder to read and detract from the overall aesthetic of the launcher.
Fix: Use a clean, sans-serif font for the "IDK Network" title that matches the rest of the launcher's design. Ensure the font is legible and has good readability at the current size.

[ISSUE #19] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: LawOfUX] [CRITERION: Jakob's Law]
Description: The "IDK Network" login modal does not follow common design patterns for login forms. For example, it lacks a "Remember me" checkbox or a "Forgot password" link.
Impact: Users may expect these common features and be confused or frustrated when they are not present.
Fix: Add common login form features such as a "Remember me" checkbox and a "Forgot password" link. Place them in a logical location, such as below the "CONNECT" button.

[ISSUE #20] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.10 Reflow]
Description: The form layout may not reflow properly at smaller screen sizes (e.g., 320px). The input fields and buttons may become too narrow or overlap.
Impact: Users on smaller screens or with zoomed-in browsers may have difficulty using the form.
Fix: Ensure the form is responsive and reflows at 320px CSS pixels. Use flexible layouts (e.g., flexbox or grid) and relative units (e.g., percentages, em, rem) to allow elements to adjust their size and position based on the screen size. Test the form at 320px to ensure no horizontal scrolling is required.

[VISUAL HIERARCHY & LAYOUT]: FAIL — Multiple issues found, including insufficient contrast, lack of focus indicators, and inconsistent button styling.
[COLOR & CONTRAST]: FAIL — Placeholder text and "REGISTER" button text have insufficient contrast.
[INTERACTIVE FEEDBACK]: FAIL — Buttons lack visible focus and hover states.
[FORM DESIGN]: FAIL — Input fields lack labels and visible focus indicators.
[NAVIGATION]: PASS — no issues found.
[LOADING & EMPTY STATES]: FAIL — No loading indicators or feedback for the "CONNECT" button.
[ERROR HANDLING]: FAIL — No error messages or validation feedback for input fields.
[RESPONSIVENESS]: FAIL — Form may not reflow properly at 320px.
[ACCESSIBILITY]: FAIL — Multiple WCAG violations, including contrast, focus, and labeling issues.
[CONSISTENCY]: FAIL — Inconsistent button colors and lack of standard login form elements.
[PERFORMANCE PERCEPTION]: FAIL — No loading indicators or feedback.
[MINIMALISM]: FAIL — Pixelated font and potential unnecessary elements.
